summary: The event-driven Standing rollup's model calls are traced: they carry a distinguishing label under a root span the fold owns, instead of being invisible or mis-rooted under whatever dispatched it.
details: The rollup fold (nora/ingest/stages/standing_event.py) called the model client directly, bypassing debrief._complete's tracing, so its two model calls carried no span at all: no model, no prompt digest, no finish_reason. Both calls now go through debrief._complete, with an honestly empty tag_id (this path has no tag) and the conversation id it does have.

_event_fold now opens its own root span (standing.event_fold, nora.trace_kind=generation) under attached(None), so it never inherits the ingest pipeline's plumbing root regardless of which of the two dispatch paths (a fresh spawn, or a slot's release_and_dispatch) started it. Before this, a fold dispatched from inside the ingest path's plumbing root was dropped entirely at the sampler, and a fold started from an empty context surfaced as an unnamed bare Strands trace.

Corrected from an earlier draft of this note: the calls do not render as `engagement.debrief.fold`/`.verdict` spans through a `generation(...)` wrapper — a later change (2026-09-19) deleted that wrapper (it was producing a second, overlapping trace on top of the Strands Agent invocation the fold actually runs through since an even earlier change, 4448c737) and replaced it with a `nora.debrief.call` attribute on the Strands-produced span, since fold/consolidate/verdict now share one Strands agent_name and can no longer be told apart by span name alone.
limitations: The verdict this path produces is still not persisted (no tag_id to key a TurnVerdict on) — only its visibility on the trace changed, not what it writes.
